items.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a Continuous Diffusion Language Model with 14 checkpoints at 3B/8B
items.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, 14 open 3B and 8B continuous diffusion language model checkpoints. Sigma denoises text in a learned 16-D embedding space, distills to few-step samplers, and decodes up to 4.20x faster than autoregressive decoding.

items.summary: Baseten released bison-1 and groundhog-1, open-weight decision models built on Gemma 4. bison-1 scores 76 on the AA Decision Index v2.1, and both models support 128k context and image input.

items.title: US technology stocks suffer their worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts pile up
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100 has slipped into a bear market after its worst weekly loss since the Covid-19 crisis. Nvidia plunged 14 percent as the SEC reviews its accounting, and Anthropic lost nearly all of its gains a day after its record IPO.

items.title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
items.summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open looped transformer that runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token. This lets the model reason internally for longer without generating extra text.

items.title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, math's most famous open problem for 167 years, with a proof formalized in Lean that spans over 250,000 pages. Just hours later, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human competing proof, and mathematicians are now checking whether either one holds up.

items.title: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live-1.1 for Voice Agents, Cuts Idle Cost to $0.02/Min
items.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-Live-1.1 in the API. The full-duplex voice model improves multilingual accents and transcription, and a new standby mode bills idle WebRTC time at $0.02 per minute instead of $0.05.

items.title: Meet Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini: 26B Looped MoE Runs on a 32GB Mac
items.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter looped MoE transformer with 3.4B active parameters. It runs on a 32GB Mac or one DGX Spark and scores 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
items.summary: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meant to fix common model behaviors such as overly brief answers, unnecessary follow-up questions, and excessive testing when coding. The API is changing as well, since editing a conversation's history can discard reasoning content and lower response quality.

items.title: Chess.com’s next move is a new hub for classic games, from mahjong to sudoku
items.summary: Chess.com is ready to go a lot bigger than chess. After launching Gambit, a gambling-free poker site, earlier this year, the company is now adding 10 more games: backgammon, checkers, go, hearts, mahjong, shogi, sudoku, solitaire, xiangqi, and a Scrabble alternative called word.

items.title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
items.summary: A Buddhist monastery in Vermont called Maple wants to establish itself as Silicon Valley's spiritual authority while creating its own AI god. According to a New Yorker report, leader Soryu Forall's group records every breath its members take to train an AI in his image.

items.title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
items.summary: Nvidia researchers argue that language models often don't need their full context windows—which are slow, expensive, and prone to errors—and propose an alternative. In tests, periodic summaries and targeted keyword search usually matched full-context results at a fraction of the cost.

items.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
items.summary: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol give much shorter, more direct answers than their predecessors, but they are also less willing to admit uncertainty. Anthropic's Claude models score well ahead on transparency.

items.title: Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries
items.summary: Google launched Gemini API Tool Retrieval in preview. Agents keep a large tool library on standby and load each parameter schema only when needed, inside one Interactions API request.

items.summary: Major US financial institutions are banning third-party bots from logging into your accounts—and warning that any costly bot mistakes are strictly your problem.

items.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items.summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct. Dozens of independent verifiers checked the 17 million lines of computer code.

items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.summary: Security researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to uncover serious vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, finding at least three compromised providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and marketplace resellers who were simply reading customer requests. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and 125 endpoints.

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.summary: METR reports that leading AI models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks but getting harder to measure. Current data can't rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development, the organization warns, though it also says common tests may overestimate what the models can actually do.
